THE ITALIAN GRAND PRIX IS COMING AND THE DRAMA IS ALREADY OVERWHELMING 🏎️

Five days. That is all that separates us from one of the most wildly anticipated Grands Prix of the 2026 season. Here is why Monza (September 4-6) is unmissable this year:

🔴 ANTONELLI STARTS FROM LAST
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli arrives at Monza having just taken a full power unit change penalty. The Mercedes rookie who has captured the F1 world's imagination will line up from the back of the grid at his home circuit. He carries a 59-point lead into the weekend — but how much of that lead will survive is a genuine question.

🟠 NORRIS IS ON FIRE
Lando Norris won the Dutch Grand Prix and has now collected back-to-back victories. He is 83 points off the championship lead, but with Antonelli compromised, Monza is Norris's best opportunity yet to dramatically reduce that gap. A win for Norris combined with a poor result for Antonelli could close things to around 58 points with 7 races remaining.

🔴 FERRARI AT HOME
Ferrari will be running their stunning Michael Schumacher tribute livery — red, black, and gold inspired by the F310 from Schumacher's first Ferrari season in 1996. The Scuderia also debuts its ADUO-2 upgraded power unit at Monza, reportedly delivering +15hp over the ADUO-1. If there was ever a time for Ferrari to win their home race, this is it.

🏁 Race: Sunday, September 6 | 2:00 PM local | 8:00 AM ET

Are you watching? This is why we love Formula 1.

FERRARI IS BRINGING THE MOST BEAUTIFUL LIVERY OF THE 2026 SEASON TO MONZA 🔴⚫🏆

For the Italian Grand Prix, Ferrari is paying tribute to Michael Schumacher with a special one-race livery on the SF-26. Here are all the details:

🏎️ THE INSPIRATION
The livery is based on the Ferrari F310 — the car Schumacher drove in his very first season with Ferrari in 1996. That was exactly 30 years ago. The F310 was red with distinctive black sidepods, and the Monza version of the SF-26 will echo that iconic color scheme.

🎨 THE DESIGN
• Predominantly red with black detailing on the sidepods
• Gold wheels — a direct callback to the F310's visual identity
• Ferrari teased the livery with a video captioned "Home is calling"

👔 THE RACE SUITS
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will wear special race suits that are predominantly red, featuring 7 stars — the same design Michael Schumacher used on his famous helmet throughout his career.

❤️ HAMILTON'S WISH
Lewis Hamilton, who has spoken publicly about wanting to race in an all-red Ferrari, is finally getting that moment. On the circuit where Ferrari's Italian roots run deepest.

Schumacher's legacy in red lives on — 30 years later, at the same circuit, in the hands of a new generation. 

What do you think of the tribute? ❤️

LANDO NORRIS IS THE HOTTEST DRIVER IN FORMULA 1 RIGHT NOW 🟠

Forget the championship standings for a second and look at what Lando Norris has done over the past two race weekends. Back-to-back victories. Including the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, a circuit where he showed stunning pace and clean execution to take a dominant win.

Now comes Monza.

Here is why this weekend matters so much for Norris:
• He is 83 points behind Antonelli in the championship
• Antonelli is starting from the BACK of the grid at Monza (power unit penalty)
• Monza is a low-downforce, high-speed circuit that historically suits cars with strong straight-line pace
• If Norris wins and Antonelli finishes outside the points, the championship gap shrinks to approximately 58 points with 7 races remaining — 175 maximum points still available

For reference: 58 points with 7 races left means the title is very much alive.

Norris is in form. Antonelli is compromised. The championship is suddenly interesting in a way it hasn't been since July.

THE MONACO GRAND PRIX PODIUM IS STILL UP IN THE AIR 🇲🇨

Here is where the Pierre Gasly Monaco appeal situation stands as of today:

📋 WHAT HAPPENED
In the Monaco Grand Prix, Gasly received a pit lane speeding penalty — along with several other drivers — based on speed measurements at Monaco's unique pitlane entrance. Alpine later filed a successful Right of Review, demonstrating that the pitlane speed measurement system had been operating incorrectly. FOM admitted the error.

Gasly was reinstated to P3. However, the complication is that other penalised drivers — like Oscar Piastri — had already served their penalties during the race, losing positions they never got back.

⚖️ THE APPEAL
Both McLaren (representing Piastri's interests) and Red Bull formally appealed Gasly's reinstatement to the FIA's International Court of Appeal (ICA). The closed-door hearing took place on August 25 in Paris, in front of a four-judge panel.

⏱️ THE TIMELINE
The judges have indicated the verdict will NOT be immediate — the case involves complex arguments about how served penalties should interact with overturned rulings. According to reports, the decision is expected in approximately two to three weeks from the hearing date (August 25), putting the verdict around mid-September.

Current status: Gasly holds P3 in the Monaco GP results. Alpine retains those championship points. Everything could change in two weeks.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 5:00 PM ET

KIMI ANTONELLI'S TITLE LEAD IS INTACT — BUT MONZA COULD TEST IT SEVERELY 🏆

The numbers are straightforward: Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship by 59 points. He has been extraordinary all season — an Italian teenager (now 20) leading a world championship in his debut season, often under enormous pressure.

But here is the thing about Monza: Antonelli will start from the very back of the grid.

Mercedes made the calculated decision to take a complete power unit change at Monza — accepting a grid penalty in exchange for fresh, reliable components for the final seven rounds of the 2026 season. The logic is sound in theory: sacrifice one race to ensure you have the best possible machinery heading into the run-in.

The math, however, is unforgiving. Starting from the back at one of F1's fastest circuits, with Lando Norris in red-hot form and Ferrari at their motivational peak on home soil, puts Antonelli in a position he has never been in before this season.

What are the scenarios?
• Antonelli fights from back to P6, Norris wins: Gap shrinks from 59 to ~34 points
• Antonelli fails to score, Norris wins: Gap closes to ~34 points (25-pt swing)
• Antonelli fights to P8, Russell or Hamilton wins: Gap shrinks, Mercedes "team" stays ahead
• Ferrari wins at home: The championship narrative completely resets

For Antonelli, this weekend is about damage limitation. For his rivals, it is the opportunity they have been waiting for all season.

September 6 cannot come soon enough.
